text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended sharply lower after spot September dived through psychological support at $1,600. By the close active September was $110 lower at $1,520 per tonne, at a discount to November of $1,540 per tonne. November shed $90 to close at $1,540 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York ended sharply lower as heavy speculative and trade selling of the nearby September/December switch, a barometer of near-term availability, kept the market under pressure for much of the day.

Traders said the high premium is drawing coffee to the market and many industry sources expect the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report to show a build in green coffee stowed in US warehouses during July.

Most early estimates look for an increase over June levels of 50,000 to 100,000 60-kg bags. Last month, GCA reported US coffee stocks rose by 139,000 bags in June, to 2.116 million bags, while in July 1996 stock piles decreased by 252,000 bags to 1.909 million bags. Another factor undermining sentiment was mild weather in Brazil.

In spite of easing concerns about nearby supply tightness it should be noted that only about 1,800 bags were pending certification on August 11 and certified coffee stocks had been creeping lower during the past few days. September lost 11.15 cents/lb to close at 188.20 cents/lb, while December gave up 6.25 cents/lb to close at 168.50 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 2.85 to 4.35 cents/lb.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 916,598 60-kg bags of coffee, ground and in beans, in July, down from 1.00 million bags exported the previous month and below the 1.16 million bags exported the same month in 1996. This brought cumulative exports since the beginning of 1997 up to 8.49 million bags, up from 4.92 million bags shipped by July 1996.

The July 1997 sales brought total earnings from coffee exports so far this year to $1.58 bln, 123 per cent higher than the $708.93 million earned in the same period in 1996. The average price per bag fell to $204.95 in July from $217.84 in June, the Brazilian Federation of Coffee Exporters (Febec) said.

BRAZIL - Coffee stocks held by Brazilian co-operatives totalled 1.77 million 60.5 kg bags on July 31, the National Coffee Council (CNC) said. This is up from 1.08 million bags held by co-operatives on June 30 but below the 2.63 million bags held at the end of July 1996.

Sales by co-operatives reached 479,805 bags in July versus 298,835 bags during June and 721,036 bags in July 1996. Co-operatives received 1.16 million bags of coffee during the month of July against 532,574 bags delivered the previous month and 1.77 million bags received in July 1996, the CNC said.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 227 bags as of August 11 to 93,565 bags. There were 1,803 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

NORWAY - Norway imported 72,634 bags of coffee in June 1997, 33 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 428,000 bags, 11 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996.

Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 8.7 per cent to 719,900 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1997 were Guatemala (68,100 vs 51,200 bags), Mexico (50,400 vs 54,400 bags), Brazil (132,800 vs 80,600 bags) and Colombia (70,700 vs 81,700 bags).
